Go and become aware of the “now” itself,
do not react to the forms that come and go.
They are all games of the mind,
there is no self of yours within them.
You go and become aware of the “now” itself,
become conscious of the ever-present now,
beyond the phenomena that occur in the now.
That is a miracle,
the shift in consciousness is a miracle.
When you realize
that you are the ever-present now,
everything becomes so simple,
and the world is no longer a problem for you.
Whatever the content of your life may be,
it is all a story about the “me” in your mind,
and you will never identify with it again.
You remember the now, and feel the now,
you remember to feel the now.
You no longer react to events,
no longer seek yourself in the stories of the past,
nor seek yourself in the fabrications of the future.
No reacting, no identifying,
and life becomes so simple and beautiful.
In the course of life, do not react to the forms that appear.

In your life, new things and new ideas keep appearing—various emotions, outer events, people playing around you, and the scenes around you constantly changing; these are all just content. Rather than reacting to the content (content is something you can be aware of), rather than merely being aware of it and identifying with what happens in the now, you go and become aware of the “now” itself, beyond the phenomena that occur in the now. That is a miracle—the shift in consciousness is a miracle.

[Identifying with what happens in the now] Taking it to be real and injecting into it a sense of self (self and other, right and wrong, benefit and harm, gain and loss, honor and disgrace, love and hate, grasping and rejecting, gratitude and grievance, intimacy and distance).

What does it mean to be able to be aware of the now? You become able to be aware of the ever-present now, upon which all things happen. You go and feel it—and not only that (that is still not quite right)—you can come to realize that you are the now itself.
Everything becomes so simple. When you understand this, you are the ever-present now, and the world is no longer a problem for you. When you understand that you are that
(the now)
, then whatever the content of your life may be, it is all a story about the self in your mind, and it will no longer be a problem. It is merely
(in the mind)
a story about “me.” You will never identify with it again
(taking it to be real, taking the protagonist in it to be you)

All that remains is your photo album—whether a physical album or the album in your mind—of the things that happened to me, well, or video recordings and such. Modern people record videos; you may have some collection from two years ago, five years ago, or ten years ago: “That is me and my first wife, that is me and my second wife, and then there was a third wife.” You would not say they are all illusions; of course they are your first, second, and third wives. It is
okay
—you no longer react to those relationships, to the events or scripts of the past.

You remember the now and feel the now; you remember to feel the now. In your life you no longer react to past relationships; you no longer seek yourself in your interactions with your ex-wife or ex-husband. This is just an example.

Those stories are over—thinking about what he or she did to me, “I will never forgive him,” and such. Those are merely things that happened, things that happened in the past, having nothing to do with me; I no longer identify with them. You no longer need to identify with them, and the future will be fine too.

Of course you need the future to handle many things—no one objects—but you no longer seek yourself in the future. You cannot find yourself in the future, so there are no problems at all. There is nothing to fear. As for the future, it is guaranteed not to have what you want—indeed so. You can accept it: you plan to do this and that next week, where to go next year, arrange some things for the future, decide what you will do—but you do not identify with them. You simply do them effortlessly, not squeezing yourself. Effort means that you are seeking yourself in certain things.
Whenever you seek the self, effort appears—stress and strain. Without effort, how simple life is! With wisdom, how simple life is!
I am not saying that life no longer has challenges—of course there will be challenges. Challenges are wonderful, but very simple, because there is only the now; nothing is a big deal.
If you can feel only the now, living in the now has power. If you can allow all the things in life to happen, then when you need a solution, power at once flows through your body and you act.

Some people encounter emergencies, and many are amazed at how they could be so—how they had the courage to do those things. There is no thought in it at all; it is as if a power took the place of themselves, and so those people say they do not know how they did it. They think they did nothing great, because it has no meaning for them.

Your life can be just like that—simple—if you continually place your attention on the feeling of the now, go and feel the feeling itself, let it happen, let the world happen. This is very good. Let forms come and go freely. No form lasts very long; every form comes and goes. Let it come. You enjoy the forms playing around you, and there is no longer any sense of fear of loss.

Why is there fear of loss? Because you have a sense of identification with certain content; you are afraid that one day, if you lose those things, you will not know who you are. That is the fear of loss. Whether it is losing a thing or any kind of loss, when you no longer care, that will be the end of fear. You can imagine what a great transformation it is—when you are no longer ruled by fear—my goodness!
You can live in a state—a state of continual joy—no matter what happens. Because whatever happens is really not that important; it is just a form. Its life is very brief; it is phenomena at play.
The universe treats forms as toys; consciousness treats forms as toys. Let them play. You yourself also join in the game. You can create without seeking what you yourself are.

When there is no “you,” you create beautifully. But when you seek the self within it, you create negative energy: “I need, I want, I must have—without those I am nothing; I cannot lose that; in this competition I must compete with him, because he may get it before me.” All of this has created our civilization.

Let it go! The power of consciousness will flow through you; it will continually create. Who knows what it will create through you—you need not know either; let it flow. Then everything in your life will be simple, in this moment. And it is always this simple.

When you no longer seek yourself in the past and the future, you can honor that one moment—honor the now and bid it farewell. Because this is life; this is the expression of life. You bid farewell to all things. Yes, through this farewell you will come to understand the space that surrounds forms—this will be a new stage of consciousness.
